newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says 1997 growth seen 7.6-8.0 percent. [CORRECTED 23:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says 1997 growth seen 7.6-8.0 percent. [CORRECTED 23:10 GMT]

text.p: Indonesia's Industry and Trade Ministry said on Thursday the country's economic growth was expected to be between 7.6 and 8.0 percent in 1997 while inflation was seen at below 7.0 percent.

It said in a statement issued during a year-end news briefing by Industry and Trade Minister Tunky Ariwibowo that the economy is expected to expand by 7.6-7.9 percent this year, with inflation seen at 6.5-6.8 percent.

The statement said the country's non-oil and gas imports were expected to total between $43.8 billion and $44.2 billion in 1997, up from an estimated total of between $39.2 billion and $39.6 billion this year.
It said non-oil and gas exports (Corrects from imports) were expected to total between $44.7 billion and $45.1 billion in 1997, compared with between $38.8 billion and $39.1 billion this year.
The statement said investment growth was expected to ease to 10.7-11.2 percent this year from 15.20 percent in 1995.
